overall_notes: Capstone clears the strict bar. Round 2 retrofits all landed: expanded_walkthrough.rationale cites Konold (2002) 'Teaching Concepts Fundamentally' and Lehrer & Schauble (2002) 'Investigating Real Data' and frames the trap as process-vs-realised-data; recovery_moves branches diagnostically into three labelled paths (DIAGNOSTIC A child says SAME MODE because 'same die'; DIAGNOSTIC B knows variability but can't articulate; DIAGNOSTIC C makes prediction but won't justify with data). Lucky+Mae capstone refrain 'Same die, different ROLLS! Different MODES! PREDICTION uses the DATA!' appears in minds_on hook AND consolidation exit_routine as call-and-response. NO-PAPER 5-corner station alternative explicitly listed in differentiation.for_movement_learners. Action step 6 is the COMPARE TWO PREDICTIONS step — Lin (SAME mode, same die) vs Sam (DIFFERENT mode, fresh sets) — with Mae adjudicating long-run vs short-run mode and citing Konold (2002) by name. Alignment Level 4: expanded_walkthrough explicitly cross-references Lessons 1-4 ('integrates Lessons 1-4: likelihood (L1), complement (L2), spinner-proportion (L3), dice-fairness (L4)'). Instructional_balance Level 4: puppets explicitly OPTIONAL with three substitutes named, plus NO-PAPER corner-station path. Mathematical_authenticity Level 4: research-grounded misconception named, children invent and compare strategies via Lin/Sam debate. Lesson_worksheet_consistency lands at Level 3 — the worksheet faithfully practices D2.1 (Part 1 likelihood + complement) and D2.2 (Part 2 spinner+dice mode, Part 3 survey + cross-group prediction) and the parts each map to a named success criterion, but the worksheet is largely a condensed mirror of the lesson stations rather than a deliberate transfer-task variation with a justified twist (early_finisher 'write WHY modes might differ' is a small nod toward extension but not the whole worksheet's design move). One Level 3 is permitted; verdict passes.
